title: Amount Still Outstanding on a Workplace Cafe Management Program Contract
content:
Credit control on a Workplace Cafe Management Program contract turns on one figure: what the client still owes against the management fees invoiced for the site. Two movements on the contract's ledger bear on it, the payments received from the client and the service credits allowed back to the client, and the window in every case is the twelve months up to the day the charge is raised.

## The clause

Where a service credit stands allowed on the contract in the twelve months up to the day the charge is raised and the payments received over those twelve months fall short of the management fees invoiced over them, the amount still outstanding is the management fees invoiced over those twelve months less both the payments received and the service credits allowed over them, rounded to the nearest cent; where no service credit stands allowed over those twelve months and the payments received fall short of the management fees invoiced over them, the amount still outstanding is the management fees invoiced over those twelve months less the payments received over them, rounded to the nearest cent; and where the payments received over those twelve months reach the management fees invoiced over them, nothing stands outstanding.

## The clause read off the ledger

Every row below reads the twelve months up to the day the charge is raised.

| What the ledger shows | The amount still outstanding |
| --- | --- |
| A service credit stands allowed, and the payments received fall short of the management fees invoiced | The management fees invoiced less both the payments received and the service credits allowed, rounded to the nearest cent |
| No service credit stands allowed, and the payments received fall short of the management fees invoiced | The management fees invoiced less the payments received, rounded to the nearest cent |
| The payments received reach the management fees invoiced | Nothing stands outstanding |

## Worked on hypothetical ledgers

Take a hypothetical ledger showing management fees invoiced of 74200.00 USD, payments received of 51800.00 USD and one service credit of 2450.00 USD allowed over those twelve months. A service credit stands allowed and the payments received fall short, so the amount still outstanding is 74200.00 USD less 51800.00 USD and less 2450.00 USD, which is 19950.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent. On the same ledger with no service credit allowed, it is 74200.00 USD less 51800.00 USD, which is 22400.00 USD, rounded to the nearest cent.

The boundary sits where the payments received meet the management fees invoiced. With hypothetical payments received of 74199.99 USD against management fees invoiced of 74200.00 USD and no service credit allowed, the payments fall short and 0.01 USD stands outstanding; with payments received of 74200.00 USD against the same management fees invoiced, they reach them and nothing stands outstanding.
